title.en: Corrugated board liners, flute direction and cut edges

summary: Make a corrugated panel read as liners around a fluted medium, especially where edges, folds and torn surfaces expose its construction.
objective: Make a corrugated panel read as liners around a fluted medium, especially where edges, folds and torn surfaces expose its construction.
intent_signals: Make a corrugated panel read as liners around a fluted medium, especially where edges, folds and torn surfaces expose its construction.
example_prompts: Build an explorable corrugated board liners, flute direction and cut edges and expose its construction at close range.

principles: Single-wall board is not a solid brown slab with stripes on every face. Its internal flute direction determines which edge cuts reveal repeated flute openings.
Separate printed liner artwork from board structure; ink does not continue through an exposed flute cavity.
implementation: For the authored single-wall preset create two liner skins and one thin corrugated medium bonded between them. Give all paper sheets finite thickness and keep the flute amplitude within the liner gap; use a rounded repeating section with one explicit axis.

Use actual cavity geometry on an exposed hero edge and a simpler bounded edge representation farther away. Keep large front faces mostly continuous; do not emboss the full flute wave onto the printed liner without an explicitly chosen surface defect.

Assign front/back printing in liner coordinates; a torn patch removes the affected liner locally and exposes the medium underneath. A crushed crease is an authored deformed region, not a prediction from paper strength. Keep cut edges, folds and glue seams as distinct features.

When constructing box flaps, carry material axes with the panel fold. Avoid coincident double walls or gaps at the fold hinge; use a finite-radius fold or a clearly schematic hinge as appropriate to the chosen style.
Compare unprinted, printed and torn patches under one light. Favor edge silhouette and paper thickness in closeups; reserve fine fibers and speckle for a scale where they remain resolved.
observable_checks: Inspect perpendicular panel edges: the chosen flute direction yields different cut profiles rather than the same repeated holes on every edge.
Hide the front liner: the medium remains a thin continuous corrugation between the rear liner and the original front contact plane.
Fold or resize a panel: liner printing follows the panel and the flute scale does not silently change unless the material preset changes.

known_limits: No box strength, crushing, moisture, insulation or recyclability certification. Flute dimensions and bend damage are authored unless a specific grade is sourced.
Authored construction and prospective checks; no runtime artifact, render or material test has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Clean white packaging, kraft board, colorful toy construction or enlarged educational flutes can use the same layer contract.

claims.statement: FEFCO describes single-wall corrugated board as a fluted paper medium glued between two liners; single-face board has only one liner.
claims.scope: Layer construction only; no numerical material property or environmental claim.
